theme: Aaron’s rod buds; priestly dues; the red heifer
readingInstruction: Read Numbers 17:1-19:22. These chapters finish the story of the challenge to Aaron, describe the duties of the priests and Levites, and give the strange law of the red heifer. Read the middle chapter for its theme of provision, and the last for its theme of cleansing.
settingTheScene: After the rebellion of Korah, the question of who may approach God has to be settled for good. Chapter 17 does this with a sign: twelve staffs are placed before the ark overnight, and only Aaron’s blossoms. Chapter 18 describes what the priests and Levites receive for their support, and chapter 19 describes a ritual for cleansing from contact with the dead, using the ashes of a red heifer.
observation: Twelve staffs, one for each tribe, are laid before the LORD in the tent of meeting (17:1-7).
“Behold, the staff of Aaron for the house of Levi had sprouted and put forth buds and produced blossoms, and it bore ripe almonds” (17:8).
The staff is put back before the testimony as a sign to the rebels (17:10).
The people cry, “Behold, we perish, we are lost, we are all lost!” (17:12).
The priests and Levites have no inheritance in the land: “I am your portion and your inheritance among the people of Israel” (18:20).
The Levites receive the tithe, and they give a tithe of the tithe to the priests (18:21-32).
A red heifer without blemish is slaughtered outside the camp, and burned with cedar, hyssop, and scarlet yarn (19:1-10).
The ashes are mixed with water to cleanse anyone who has touched a dead body (19:11-22).
interpretation:
Aaron’s staff is a picture of life from death. A dry stick, cut from a tree, put in a dark tent overnight, bursts into buds, flowers, and ripe almonds. It is a miracle that shows the choice of God, and it also gives a symbol of resurrection. The staff was dead wood, and it lived. The one God has chosen is the one who brings life.

The sign settles the question, and it also shows the people’s fear. They had been grumbling that Moses and Aaron were killing them, and now they say, “We are lost!” The proper answer to that fear is in the next chapter, where God sets out the provision for the priesthood. The priests will bear the iniquity of the sanctuary. They stand between God’s holiness and the people’s sin, so that the people do not die by coming too near.

The statement in 18:20 is one of the loveliest in the book. The priests and Levites will have no land. “I am your portion and your inheritance.” It sounds like a loss, but it is the greatest gift. The ones closest to God have God himself. The psalmist later says, “The LORD is my chosen portion and my cup” (Psalm 16:5).

The red heifer is the most puzzling ritual in the law. It involves a spotless animal sacrificed outside the camp, burned, and its ashes used for cleansing. It is a rite for dealing with death, the great defilement. A priest who prepares the ashes becomes unclean himself, a paradox that the rabbis later noted. The one who cleanses others is made unclean by the work.

The common thread through these chapters is that God provides what is needed to live in his presence. He provides a priest who is chosen and living, a portion that is himself, and a cleansing for the effects of death. Each of these looks ahead to Christ.
connection: Jesus is the one who rose from the dead, the true budding rod. Hebrews 9:13-14 says, “If the blood of goats and bulls, and the sprinkling of defiled persons with the ashes of a heifer, sanctify for the purification of the flesh, how much more will the blood of Christ… purify our conscience from dead works.” Hebrews 13:12 says that Jesus suffered outside the gate. Paul says that Christ is “the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep” (1 Corinthians 15:20).
application:
Reflect on the statement, “I am your portion.” Ask whether God himself is enough for you.

Thank God for the life that comes out of death, in Christ and in your own story.

Read Hebrews 9:13-14 and pray for the cleansing of your conscience from dead works.
prayerPrompts: Tell God what it means that he is your portion and inheritance.
Thank him for the life that comes out of death in Jesus.
Ask him to cleanse your conscience and let you live without fear.
